title: Authentication and authorization
summary: Read the authenticated identity, then define roles and request permissions.

richText: The authenticated user
After authentication, Spring stores an Authentication object in the SecurityContext.
The principal is the authenticated identity. Granted authorities are the permissions attached to that identity.
For password login, UserDetailsService loads the user and stored password hash. The authentication provider checks the password with PasswordEncoder.
Controllers can receive the authenticated Principal as a method parameter. Read identity from this server-controlled authentication, rather than a user ID supplied by the caller.
Roles and authorities
An authority is a permission name, such as journal:read.
A role groups users, such as USER or ADMIN. Spring represents roles as authorities with the ROLE_ prefix by default.
roles("ADMIN") adds ROLE_ADMIN to the user. hasRole("ADMIN") checks that authority.
hasAuthority("journal:read") checks the exact permission name.
A username such as admin does not automatically give the ADMIN role.
Rules for HTTP requests
permitAll() allows a request without login.
authenticated() requires authentication.
hasRole(...) and hasAuthority(...) require the named permission.
denyAll() rejects the request.
Spring applies the first matching request rule. Put specific paths before a broad fallback.

example.title: Allow public routes and restrict admin routes
description: Add this bean to a @Configuration class in a Spring Boot 3 application.
Import Bean, HttpSecurity, SecurityFilterChain and Customizer.
Configure UserDetailsService and PasswordEncoder as shown in the security basics lesson.
The existing application has public, admin and journal endpoints.
explanation: The /public/** rule allows visitors who have not logged in.
The /admin/** rule requires ROLE_ADMIN. A user with only ROLE_USER is denied.
The /journal/** rule accepts any authenticated user. It does not check which journal entry that user owns.
The final rule denies paths not covered above.
The filter chain checks access before the controller runs.

richText: Rules for service methods
Use @EnableMethodSecurity on a configuration class to enable method authorization.
@PreAuthorize checks a rule before a method runs.
@PreAuthorize("hasRole('ADMIN')") requires ADMIN for calls through the Spring-managed proxy.
Calling a secured method directly from another method in the same object bypasses this proxy check.
Responses when access fails
An API normally returns 401 for missing or invalid authentication.
An authenticated user without the required permission normally receives 403.
Browser form login can redirect an unauthenticated request to the login page.
